easy.def: A thin ball of liquid filled with air.
examples: I blow bubbles.
The bubble popped.
The soap made bubbles.

more.def: A very thin ball of liquid with air or gas inside.
examples: I blew a big bubble with the wand.
The bubbles floated away and popped.
Bubbles rose to the top of the water.

easy.def: A male deer.
examples: A buck stood in the field.
The buck has antlers.
We saw a buck in the woods.

more.def: A male deer, rabbit or goat.
examples: The buck lifted its head and listened.
A buck's antlers can grow quite large.
The buck led the herd across the field.

easy.def: A dollar.
examples: It costs five bucks.
I found a buck.
Dad gave me ten bucks.

more.def: An informal word for one dollar.
examples: The sticker cost only a buck.
That toy costs ten bucks.
She earned five bucks for washing the car.

easy.def: A round container with a handle for carrying water.
examples: I fill the bucket.
The bucket is full of sand.
I carried the bucket.

more.def: A deep, round container with a handle, used for carrying liquids or sand.
examples: I filled the bucket with water.
The kids carried buckets of sand to the castle.
Rain dripped into a bucket.

easy.def: A metal piece that closes a belt.
examples: My belt has a buckle.
The buckle is shiny.
The shoe has a buckle.

more.def: A metal clasp that fastens a belt or strap.
examples: My belt has a shiny buckle.
The buckle on my shoe came loose.
The pilgrim hat had a big buckle.

easy.def: To close a belt or strap.
examples: Buckle your seat belt.
I buckled my shoe.
She buckled her helmet.

more.def: To fasten something with a metal clasp.
examples: Buckle your seat belt before we go.
I buckled my sandal.
She buckled the strap on her helmet.

easy.def: A friend.
examples: My buddy and I play ball.
He is my buddy.
Buddies share snacks.

more.def: A close friend.
examples: My buddy and I ride bikes to school every day.
The two buddies built a fort in the backyard.
Swim with a buddy, not alone.

easy.def: A plan for spending money.
examples: We have a budget.
The budget is small.
Mom made a budget.

more.def: A plan that shows how much money you have and how you will spend it.
examples: Mom made a budget for the month.
Our class has a small budget for the party.
He stayed within his budget at the store.

easy.def: A meal where you pick your own food from a long table.
examples: We ate at a buffet.
The buffet had many foods.
I took pasta from the buffet.

more.def: A meal in which people serve themselves from a table of many different dishes.
examples: At the wedding buffet, guests served themselves salads, pasta and fruit.
The hotel had a breakfast buffet with eggs, fruit and pancakes.
We filled our plates at the buffet and found a table.

easy.def: A small insect.
examples: A bug crawled on me.
I saw a bug.
The bug is small.

more.def: A small insect or crawling creature.
examples: A bug crawled across the leaf.
We found a beetle bug in the garden.
Ladybugs are helpful bugs in the garden.

easy.def: A mistake in a computer program.
examples: The game has a bug.
There is a bug in the code.
The bug made it crash.

more.def: A mistake in a computer program that makes it work wrongly.
examples: The bug made the game freeze.
She fixed the bug in the program.
A bug in the code stopped the game.

easy.def: To make something by putting parts together.
examples: We build a sandcastle.
Dad built a shed.
Birds build nests.

more.def: To make something, such as a house or bridge, by putting parts together.
examples: Workers will build a new bridge.
Beavers build dams from sticks and mud.
We built a fort out of couch cushions.

easy.def: A place with walls and a roof.
examples: The building is tall.
Our school building is old.
A new building is by the park.

more.def: A structure with walls and a roof, such as a house, school or shop.
examples: The tallest building in town has twenty floors.
Our school building has a big red door.
Workers are painting the old building.

easy.def: The glass part of a light.
examples: The bulb is bright.
I changed the bulb.
The bulb burned out.

more.def: The glass part of a lamp that gives off light when electricity flows through it.
examples: I changed the light bulb.
A new bulb lit the dim hallway.
The bulb glowed in the dark.

easy.def: A round root that grows into a plant.
examples: I planted a tulip bulb.
The bulb is under the soil.
A bulb grows into a flower.

more.def: A round, thick part under the ground from which a plant such as a tulip grows.
examples: I planted tulip bulbs in the fall.
The onion is a bulb.
The bulb bloomed in spring.

easy.def: A male cow.
examples: The bull is big.
The bull has horns.
A bull stood in the field.

more.def: An adult male of the cattle family.
examples: The bull stood in the field.
A bull has a strong, heavy body.
Farmers keep the bull in a fenced pen.

easy.def: A strong dog with a wide face.
examples: The bulldog snored.
A bulldog is strong.
We have a bulldog.

more.def: A strong dog with a wide head, a flat face and loose skin.
examples: The bulldog snored on the rug.
A bulldog has short legs and a wide chest.
Our bulldog loves to play.

easy.def: A small metal piece shot from a gun.
examples: The bullet is tiny.
A bullet is very dangerous.
Police found a bullet.

more.def: A small piece of metal that is shot from a gun.
examples: The museum displayed a bullet from an old war.
Hunters must handle bullets with great care.
The officer found a bullet on the ground.

easy.def: A small dot used to mark items in a list.
examples: Put a bullet before each item.
The list has four bullets.
Each bullet gives one reason.

more.def: A small dot placed before each item in a list.
examples: Each bullet on the slide gives one reason.
She put a bullet before every item on the list.
The list had five bullets.

easy.def: A short message that tells the news.
examples: The news bulletin said it would snow.
A bulletin was on the board.
I read the bulletin.

more.def: A short news report or announcement, or a paper that lists news.
examples: The radio bulletin said that it would snow tonight.
A bulletin on the board listed the school events.
The weather bulletin warned about heavy rain.

easy.def: A person who is mean to others on purpose.
examples: The bully was mean.
Do not be a bully.
Tell a teacher about the bully.

more.def: A person who keeps picking on others who are weaker.
examples: A bully teased the smaller kids on the playground.
The teacher helped the child who was upset by the bully.
The bully was told to stop.

easy.def: To be mean to someone again and again.
examples: Do not bully others.
He bullied the boy.
Bullying is wrong.

more.def: To keep hurting or scaring someone who is weaker.
examples: It is wrong to bully other kids.
He was bullied at school until the teacher stepped in.
Bullying makes people feel sad and afraid.

easy.def: Something that lets you down.
examples: It is a bummer that it rained.
What a bummer!
Missing the party was a bummer.

more.def: Something that is annoying or disappointing.
examples: It was a bummer when the picnic was rained out.
What a bummer that the store is closed!
Missing the party was a real bummer.

easy.def: To hit something lightly.
examples: I bumped my head.
The cars bump.
He bumped the table.

more.def: To knock into something, or to hit it lightly by accident.
examples: I bumped my knee on the table.
The two shopping carts bumped.
She bumped into her friend in the hall.

easy.def: A small round place that sticks up.
examples: I have a bump on my head.
The road has a bump.
We felt a bump.

more.def: A small, round lump that sticks up, or the feeling of hitting something.
examples: The bike went over a bump in the road.
I got a bump on my knee.
We felt a bump when the plane landed.

easy.def: The bar on the front and back of a car that helps protect it.
examples: The bumper is shiny.
A sticker is on the bumper.
The bumper hit the post.

more.def: A bar on the front or back of a car that protects it from damage.
examples: A sticker was on the back bumper of the car.
The bumper was dented after it hit the fence.
Bumper cars have rubber bumpers to keep you safe.

easy.def: The soft padding along the sides of a baby's bed.
examples: The crib has a bumper.
The bumper is soft.
The baby has a bumper.

more.def: Soft padding or a rubber edge that protects something from bumps.
examples: The bowling alley put up bumpers so we would not hit the gutter.
The crib bumper kept the baby safe.
Rubber bumpers line the sides of the pinball table.

easy.def: Full of bumps.
examples: The road is bumpy.
We had a bumpy ride.
The path was bumpy.

more.def: Full of bumps, or shaking up and down.
examples: The road was bumpy, and we bounced in our seats.
We had a bumpy ride in the old truck.
The plane hit some bumpy air and shook.

easy.def: A small, round, soft bread.
examples: The burger is in a bun.
I ate a sweet bun.
The bun is warm.

more.def: A small, round, soft roll of bread, sometimes sweet.
examples: The burger came in a toasted bun.
I ate a cinnamon bun.
She tied her hair in a bun.

easy.def: A group of things together.
examples: A bunch of grapes.
A bunch of flowers.
A bunch of kids ran by.

more.def: A number of things that are tied or growing together.
examples: She picked a bunch of daisies for her mom.
He ate a bunch of grapes.
A bunch of kids ran to the playground.

easy.def: A group of things tied together.
examples: Dad had a bundle of sticks.
Mom gave me a bundle of clean socks.
The baby is in a bundle of blankets.

more.def: A number of things tied or wrapped together.
examples: She carried a bundle of newspapers under her arm.
He tied the old letters in a bundle with string.
The farmer stacked bundles of hay in the barn.

easy.def: A narrow bed built above another.
examples: I sleep in the top bunk.
The bunk has a ladder.
Bunks are in the cabin.

more.def: One of a pair of narrow beds that are built one above the other.
examples: I sleep in the top bunk at camp.
The bottom bunk is closer to the floor.
The cabin has four bunks.

easy.def: A strong underground shelter.
examples: They hid in the bunker.
The bunker is underground.
The bunker was safe.

more.def: A strong shelter that is built underground, to protect people.
examples: The family stayed in the bunker during the storm.
The bunker had thick concrete walls.
Supplies were stored in the bunker.

easy.def: A baby or pet rabbit.
examples: The bunny hopped.
I have a pet bunny.
The bunny has soft fur.

more.def: A word for a rabbit, often used for a young or small one.
examples: The bunny nibbled a carrot.
A tiny bunny hopped across the garden.
She petted the soft bunny.

easy.def: A heavy load.
examples: The donkey carried a heavy burden.
The burden was too much.
He felt the burden.

more.def: Something heavy that you have to carry, or a worry that is hard to bear.
examples: The donkey carried a heavy burden up the hill.
Too much homework can feel like a burden.
She shared the burden of the work with her sister.

easy.def: A round sandwich with a flat piece of cooked meat.
examples: I eat a burger.
The burger is hot.
Dad made burgers.

more.def: A sandwich with a round, flat patty of meat inside a bun.
examples: Dad grilled burgers for dinner.
I put ketchup on my burger.
The burger came with a pickle.

easy.def: A person who breaks into a house to steal.
examples: The burglar was caught.
A burglar broke in.
The police found the burglar.

more.def: A person who breaks into a building to steal things.
examples: The police caught the burglar.
A burglar broke a window.
The alarm scared the burglar away.

easy.def: When someone breaks into a place to steal things.
examples: There was a burglary at the shop.
A burglary happened on our street.
The police came after the burglary.

more.def: The crime of going into a building to steal things.
examples: There was a burglary at the shop last night, and the police came to look.
A burglary on our street made neighbors lock their doors.
The alarm went off during the burglary.

easy.def: Big, strong and heavy.
examples: The burly man lifted the box.
A burly bear.
He is burly.

more.def: Large, strong and heavy in build.
examples: The burly man lifted the heavy box with ease.
A burly bear stood on its hind legs.
The burly carpenter carried a stack of boards.

easy.def: To be on fire.
examples: The wood burns.
The candle is burning.
Paper burns fast.

more.def: To be on fire and give off heat and light.
examples: Logs burned in the fireplace all evening.
The candle burned with a small, steady flame.
Dry leaves burn quickly.

easy.def: To hurt something with heat.
examples: Do not burn your hand.
I burned my tongue on the soup.
The sun can burn your skin.

more.def: To hurt or damage something with heat, sun or fire.
examples: Put on sunscreen so the sun does not burn your skin.
She burned her tongue on the hot soup.
The toast burned in the toaster.

easy.def: A hole in the ground where an animal lives.
examples: The rabbit ran into its burrow.
A mole lives in a burrow.
The snake hid in a burrow.

more.def: A hole or tunnel that an animal digs in the ground to live in.
examples: The fox kept her cubs safe in a burrow under the hill.
Prairie dogs dig burrows with many rooms.
The owl made its nest in an empty burrow.

easy.def: To break open suddenly.
examples: The balloon will burst.
The pipe burst.
Water burst through the dam.

more.def: To break open suddenly, or to start something suddenly.
examples: The balloon burst with a loud pop.
The pipe burst in the cold weather.
She burst out laughing at the joke.

easy.def: To cover something with dirt.
examples: The dog buried a bone.
Pirates bury treasure.
We buried seeds.

more.def: To put something in the ground and cover it up.
examples: The dog buried its bone under the bush.
Squirrels bury nuts in the fall.
Pirates buried treasure on the island.

easy.def: A big vehicle with many seats.
examples: I ride the bus.
The bus is yellow.
We take the bus to school.

more.def: A large vehicle with many seats that carries people along a set route.
examples: The school bus stops at our corner.
We took the city bus to the museum.
The bus was full of excited kids.

easy.def: A small plant with many branches.
examples: A bird sits in the bush.
The bush has red berries.
The rabbit hid in the bush.

more.def: A woody plant that is smaller than a tree and has many stems growing from the ground.
examples: A rabbit hid under the berry bush.
The rose bush is covered in flowers.
We trimmed the bushes along the fence.

easy.def: A place that sells things or does jobs for money.
examples: My aunt has a business.
The bakery is a business.
Dad's business is small.

more.def: A shop, company, or other group that makes money by selling things or doing work.
examples: My uncle started a business that repairs bicycles.
The small business on our street sells flowers.
Many businesses close on holidays.

easy.def: A man who works in business.
examples: The businessman carried a briefcase.
My uncle is a businessman.
The businessman made a deal.

more.def: A man whose work is running or helping to run a company.
examples: The businessman gave a talk to the class.
My uncle is a businessman who sells cars.
The businessman signed the deal.

easy.def: A statue of someone's head and shoulders.
examples: The bust was made of stone.
A bust of a king.
The bust sat on the shelf.

more.def: A statue of a person's head, neck and shoulders.
examples: The museum has a stone bust of a king.
A bust of the writer sat on the desk.
The sculptor made a bust of the mayor.

easy.def: To break.
examples: The toy busted.
Do not bust the window.
The balloon busted.

more.def: To break or burst, an informal word.
examples: The toy busted when it hit the floor.
The pipe busted in the cold.
I busted my kite string.

easy.def: Lots of busy activity.
examples: The market was full of bustle.
The bustle of the city.
We heard the bustle.

more.def: Busy, noisy activity with many people moving about.
examples: Amid the bustle of the station, we found our train.
We enjoyed the bustle of the city.
There was a lot of bustle before the party.

easy.def: Having a lot to do.
examples: Mom is busy now.
I am busy with my homework.
The bee is busy.

more.def: Having a lot to do, or doing something right now.
examples: Mom is busy making dinner.
Bees are busy all summer long.
She was too busy to talk.

easy.def: Full of people or cars.
examples: The street is busy.
The store is busy today.
The park was busy.

more.def: Full of people, activity or noise.
examples: The market is busy on Saturdays.
A busy road runs by our school.
The airport was busy before the holiday.

easy.def: A word used to show something is different.
examples: I am small, but I am strong.
I like cake, but I do not like pie.
It is sunny, but it is cold.

more.def: A word used to join two ideas when the second one is a surprise or is the opposite of the first.
examples: The soup smelled wonderful, but it was too hot to eat.
He wanted to stay up late, but he fell asleep on the couch.
Bats have wings, but they are mammals and not birds.

easy.def: A person who cuts and sells meat.
examples: The butcher sold sausage.
The butcher wears an apron.
The butcher shop is small.

more.def: A person whose job is to cut up and sell meat.
examples: The butcher cut the meat for us.
We bought sausages from the butcher.
The butcher wore a white apron.

easy.def: A servant who takes care of a big house.
examples: The butler opened the door.
The butler wore a suit.
A butler served tea.

more.def: The chief servant in a large house, who answers the door and serves meals.
examples: The butler opened the door for the guests.
The butler carried a tray of tea.
In the story, the butler knew all the secrets.

easy.def: A soft yellow food you spread on bread.
examples: I put butter on my bread.
The butter is soft.
Mom spread butter on the toast.

more.def: A soft, yellow food made from cream that people spread on bread or use in cooking.
examples: She spread butter on the warm toast.
Mom melted butter in the pan to cook the eggs.
Butter turns to liquid when it gets hot.

related.def: Like butter or full of butter.

easy.def: An insect with big, colorful wings.
examples: The butterfly landed on a flower.
A butterfly has wings.
I saw a butterfly.

more.def: A flying insect with large, colorful wings that comes from a caterpillar.
examples: A butterfly drifted past the window.
A caterpillar turns into a butterfly.
Monarch butterflies fly very far.

easy.def: A small round piece that you push or fasten.
examples: Press the button.
My coat has a button.
The button fell off.

more.def: A small round object sewn on clothes to fasten them.
examples: A button fell off my coat.
She sewed a button on the shirt.
He fastened every button.

easy.def: A small part that you press to make something work.
examples: Push the button.
Press the red button.
Click the button.

more.def: A small part that you press to make a machine or game work.
examples: Push the button to start the elevator.
Press the red button to stop.
Click the button on the screen.

easy.def: To get something by paying money.
examples: I buy a toy.
Mom bought milk.
We buy fruit here.

more.def: To get something by paying money for it.
examples: We went to the store to buy a birthday card.
My sister bought a new backpack for school.
He saved up to buy a telescope.

easy.def: A person who buys something.
examples: The buyer paid.
A buyer came to see the house.
The buyer chose a red coat.

more.def: A person who buys something.
examples: The buyer paid for the car with cash.
A buyer came to see our old couch.
The shop welcomes every buyer.

easy.def: To make a humming sound like a bee.
examples: The bee buzzes.
The fly buzzed around.
My phone buzzed.

more.def: To make a low, steady humming sound.
examples: Bees buzzed around the flowers.
The alarm clock buzzed loudly.
The room buzzed with excited voices.

easy.def: A low humming sound.
examples: I hear a buzz.
The buzz of bees was loud.
The fridge made a buzz.

more.def: A low, steady humming sound like the one a bee makes.
examples: The buzz of the bees grew louder as we got close.
The buzz of the alarm woke me up.
A buzz of voices filled the cafeteria.

easy.def: A thing that makes a loud buzzing sound.
examples: Press the buzzer.
The buzzer sounded.
I heard the buzzer.

more.def: A device that makes a loud buzzing sound as a signal.
examples: Press the buzzer if you know the answer.
The buzzer sounded to end the game.
The oven buzzer told us the cookies were ready.
